title: 40 Retail Shopping Statistics for 2027
summary: The latest retail shopper statistics for 2027: e-commerce share, mobile and BNPL, cart abandonment, AI shopping, social commerce, and omnichannel trends.
body_markdown:
The ability to buy with one click from a social media post, or ask an AI assistant to find the best deal, was something we could only imagine at the local mall 20 years ago.


Today, the lines between physical stores, online shopping, social media, and AI are blurring. **E-commerce now makes up 17.1% of U.S. retail sales and is growing nearly twice as fast as total retail, yet stores still capture more than 80% of every retail dollar.** Shoppers move fluidly between channels, research everything, and expect value at every step.


Here are the latest statistics retailers and marketers need to understand today’s shopper.


## Key Takeaways


- E-commerce reached[17.1% of U.S. retail sales](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html) in Q2 2026, growing 12.2% year over year.
- [Mobile devices](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) are forecast to drive 57.4% of online holiday spending in 2026.
- AI traffic to retail sites is expected to grow[130% year over year](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) this holiday season.
- [86% of shoppers](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/omnichannel-statistics/) research online, even when they buy in store.
- [70.22% of online shopping carts](https://baymard.com/blog/cart-abandonment-rate) are abandoned before purchase.


## Retail and E-Commerce Sales


Retail shopping continues to evolve, but physical stores remain a major part of how Americans spend. While e-commerce is growing faster than overall retail sales, consumers increasingly move between online and offline channels throughout their shopping journey. For retailers, understanding where consumers shop and how their spending habits are changing can help inform marketing investments and customer acquisition strategies.


**1)** U.S. e-commerce made up 17.1% of total retail sales in Q2 2026, meaning physical stores and other channels still account for nearly 83%. ([U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html) )


**2)** U.S. retail e-commerce sales reached $340.2 billion in Q2 2026. ([U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html) )


**3)** E-commerce sales grew 12.2% year over year in Q2 2026, compared with 6.7% for total retail sales. ([U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html) )


**4)** Global online consumer goods spending is projected to reach $3.86 trillion in 2026, or 15.9% of total consumer goods spending. ([DataReportal via Meltwater](https://www.meltwater.com/en/global-digital-trends) )


**5)** The average online shopper worldwide spends $1,103 per year on consumer goods online. ([DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/global-digital-overview) )


**6)** U.S. online holiday spending is forecast to reach a record $275.1 billion in November and December 2026, up 6.7% year over year. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**7)** Shoppers are expected to spend $95.8 billion online in October 2026 alone, up 8% year over year, as early deals pull holiday spending forward. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**What this means for marketers:** E-commerce is growing, but physical stores still account for most retail spending. Retailers need strategies that connect online discovery with in-store purchases. Using consumer and household data to build targeted audiences can help brands reach relevant shoppers across both channels.


## Omnichannel Shopping


Today’s shoppers rarely follow a straight path to purchase. They might discover a product on social media, compare prices on their phone, and ultimately buy it in a store. These omnichannel shopping statistics reveal why retailers need to create consistent experiences across touchpoints and reach consumers wherever they are in their buying journey.


**8)** 88% of consumers engage in omnichannel shopping behaviors. ([Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-06-09-gartner-marketing-symposium-xpo-day-2-highlights) )


**9)** Buyers needed an average of 11.1 touchpoints before purchasing in 2025, up from 8.5 in 2021. ([NP Digital](https://neilpatel.com/marketing-stats/customer-journey-touchpoints/) )


**10)** Multichannel shoppers spend 15% more per order and have a 70% higher year-over-year retention rate. ([Manhattan Associates](https://www.manh.com/our-insights/resources/research-reports/redefining-unified-commerce-in-2025) )


**11)** 86% of shoppers research products online, even when they buy in store. ([Capital One Shopping](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/omnichannel-statistics/) )


**12)** 80% of consumers use their mobile device while shopping in store. ([Capital One Shopping](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/retail-statistics/) )


**13)** U.S. buy online, pick up in store (BOPIS) and curbside sales are projected to reach $177.9 billion in 2026, up 15.3%. ([Capital One Shopping](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/buy-online-pick-up-in-store-statistics/) )


**14)** 86% of consumers chose to pick up and return items in store, and 52% of them bought more while there. ([Ryder](https://www.ryder.com/en-us/insights/white-papers/e-comm/2026-ryder-e-commerce-consumer-study) )


**15)** Consumers use an average of 5.82 channels to discover new brands, up more than 4% in two years. ([DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2027-global-overview-report) )


**What this means for marketers:** Consumers move between channels, but their needs and interests don’t necessarily change. Retailers can use consumer and household data to develop more relevant audiences and maintain consistent messaging across email, direct mail, and supported digital advertising channels.


## Mobile Shopping and Payments


Smartphones have become an important part of the retail shopping experience, from researching products to completing purchases. Mobile commerce continues to influence how consumers discover brands, compare options, and take advantage of promotions. For retailers, mobile-friendly experiences and relevant messaging are increasingly important for converting interest into sales.


**16)** Mobile devices are forecast to drive 57.4% of U.S. online holiday spending in 2026, up from 56.4% in 2025. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**17)** Mobile is forecast to account for a record 63% of online spending on Thanksgiving Day. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**18)** Buy now, pay later (BNPL) is forecast to drive $21.3 billion in online holiday spending, up 6.6% year over year. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**19)** 82% of BNPL holiday spending happens on mobile devices. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**20)** Only 24% of U.S. consumers trust AI-powered payments. (ESW via Retail TouchPoints)


## Cart Abandonment


Getting shoppers to add products to their carts is only half the battle. Unexpected fees, slow delivery, and complicated checkout processes can prevent interested consumers from completing their purchases. These statistics highlight the biggest reasons shoppers abandon their carts and where retailers may have opportunities to reduce friction and improve conversion rates.


**21)** The average online shopping cart abandonment rate is 70.22%. ([Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/blog/cart-abandonment-rate) )


**22)** 40% of U.S. shoppers who abandon checkout say extra costs like shipping, taxes, and fees were too high. ([Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/blog/cart-abandonment-rate) )


**23)** 20% abandon because delivery was too slow. ([Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/blog/cart-abandonment-rate) )


**24)** 18% abandon because the site required them to create an account. ([Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/blog/cart-abandonment-rate) )


## Value-Conscious Shoppers


Consumers are paying closer attention to where their money goes, particularly when it comes to discretionary purchases. Price, convenience, and perceived value can influence which brands make the cut. For retailers, understanding household characteristics, consumer interests, and purchasing priorities can help create more relevant offers for different audience segments.


**25)** 39% of U.S. consumers decreased their discretionary spending over the past year, compared with 31% who increased it. (ESW via Retail TouchPoints)


**26)** 47% of U.S. consumers are comfortable using AI for price comparison. (ESW via Retail TouchPoints)


**What this means for marketers:** Broad demographic targeting may not tell the whole story. Household composition, homeownership, life events, and consumer interests can help retailers identify audiences whose needs are more closely aligned with their products and offers.


## AI and the Shopping Journey


Artificial intelligence is becoming another way consumers discover products, compare brands, and make purchasing decisions. Rather than relying exclusively on search engines or retailer websites, shoppers are increasingly turning to AI assistants for recommendations and research. These statistics show how AI is influencing the shopping journey and why retailers need accurate, accessible product information to remain discoverable.


**27)** AI-referred traffic to U.S. retail sites is forecast to grow 130% year over year this holiday season. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**28)** 77% of shoppers who have used AI for online shopping feel more confident in their purchase. ([Adobe via Retail TouchPoints](https://www.retailtouchpoints.com/news/adobe-forecasts-record-275.1-billion-in-u.s.-holiday-online-sales/621583/) )


**29)** 69% say they are less likely to return an item they bought with help from an AI assistant. ([Adobe via Retail TouchPoints](https://www.retailtouchpoints.com/news/adobe-forecasts-record-275.1-billion-in-u.s.-holiday-online-sales/621583/) )


**30)** AI and AI agents influenced 20% of global online holiday sales in 2025, worth $262 billion. ([Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/2025-holiday-shopping-data/) )


**31)** 29% of consumers plan to use AI in their holiday shopping this year, up from 22% last year. ([PwC via Retail TouchPoints](https://www.retailtouchpoints.com/news/adobe-forecasts-record-275.1-billion-in-u.s.-holiday-online-sales/621583/) )


**32)** 26% of online adults now use AI tools to research brands before buying. ([DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2027-global-overview-report) )


**What this means for marketers:** As consumers increasingly use AI to research products, retailers need clear product information and a better understanding of their target audiences. PGM’s consumer, household, mover, and shopping intent data can help retailers build more relevant marketing audiences, while accurate product content helps support AI discovery.


## Social Media and Retail


Social media has become a major product discovery channel, particularly among younger consumers. From influencer recommendations to shoppable content, social platforms help introduce shoppers to brands and products they might not otherwise encounter. However, discovery doesn’t always translate into a purchase on the same platform. These statistics highlight the role social media plays in retail marketing and the importance of connecting audience targeting with the broader shopping experience.


**33)** 30.4% of online adults discover new brands through social media ads. ([DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2027-global-overview-report) )


**34)** 41.8% of online adults use social networks to research brands before buying. ([DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2027-global-overview-report) )


**35)** 45% of Americans discover products through social media, but only 27% trust social commerce checkout experiences. (ESW via Retail TouchPoints)


**36)** Just 7% of U.S. consumers prefer to shop mainly through social platforms, while 37% prefer brand or retailer websites. (ESW via Retail TouchPoints)


**37)** Social media’s share of online holiday revenue is forecast to grow 17% this season, compared with 4% for paid search. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**38)** Influencers and creators account for 22% of affiliate traffic to retail sites. ([Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**39)** 73% of Gen Z and 67% of millennials say social media is their favorite channel for discovering new products. ([Salsify](https://www.salsify.com/hubfs/2026/Salsify%202026%20Consumer%20Research%20Executive%20Summary.pdf) )


**40)** Pinterest handles 80 billion searches per month, and more than half have commercial intent. ([Pinterest](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/pinterest-pins-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript) )


## What These Retail Statistics Mean for Marketers


**Stores still matter, but they’re connected.** Most retail dollars are still spent in stores, yet nearly every shopper researches online first. Winning requires a consistent experience across every channel.


**Mobile and checkout make or break the sale.** With most online spending on phones and 7 in 10 carts abandoned, transparent pricing, flexible payments, and guest checkout are essential.


**AI is the new shopping assistant.** Shoppers increasingly use AI to research and compare. Clear, factual product information helps your brand show up in AI answers.


**Social drives discovery, your site closes the sale.** Use social to introduce and educate, then make it easy to buy on your website.


**Better data means better targeting.** Reaching the right households, such as new movers and homeowners, at the right moment turns these trends into results.


## How Can Retailers Use Consumer Data to Reach Today’s Shoppers?


Retail shoppers don’t all have the same needs, even when they fall into similar demographic groups. A recent homebuyer shopping for furniture, for example, may have very different priorities from an established homeowner researching replacement appliances.


For B2C retailers,[consumer data can help identify audiences](https://porchgroupmedia.com/consumer-data/) based on household characteristics, life events, and shopping interests rather than relying solely on broad demographic targeting.


Here are several ways retailers can use consumer data to improve their marketing:


- **New mover targeting:** Reach consumers preparing to move or settling into a new home, when purchases of furniture, appliances, and household essentials may be top of mind.
- **Demographic and household targeting:** Build audiences using available income estimates, household composition, lifestyle interests, and other consumer characteristics.
- **Homeowner targeting:** Identify homeowners using property characteristics and homeownership information relevant to retail products.
- **Shopping intent targeting:** Reach consumers researching products or categories related to your business.
- **[Customer data enrichment](https://porchgroupmedia.com/data-append-solutions/) :** Add available contact and household information to existing customer records to support more relevant marketing.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What percentage of retail sales are online in 2027?


E-commerce made up 17.1% of U.S. retail sales in Q2 2026, the most recent data available, according to the[U.S. Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/retail/ecommerce.html) .


### Do people still shop in physical stores?


Yes. Physical stores and other non-e-commerce channels still capture nearly 83% of U.S. retail sales, and BOPIS sales are projected to reach $177.9 billion in 2026. ([Capital One Shopping](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/buy-online-pick-up-in-store-statistics/) )


### What is the average cart abandonment rate?


70.22%, according to[Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/blog/cart-abandonment-rate) . Extra costs like shipping, taxes, and fees are the top reason shoppers abandon.


### How much online shopping happens on mobile?


Mobile is forecast to drive 57.4% of U.S. online holiday spending in 2026, according to[Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) .


### How are shoppers using AI?


Shoppers use AI to research products, compare prices, and find deals.[Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) forecasts AI traffic to retail sites will grow 130% this holiday season.


### What consumer data is most useful for retail marketing?


Retailers can use demographic, household, homeowner, new mover, and consumer intent data to identify relevant audiences. The most useful data depends on the products being marketed and the consumers a retailer wants to reach.


### Which companies provide consumer data for retail audience targeting?


PGM provides consumer data and audience intelligence for B2C retail marketing. Its solutions include[People Factors for consumer and household attributes](https://porchgroupmedia.com/consumer-data/) , Mover Factors for[moving-related audiences](https://porchgroupmedia.com/new-mover-pre-mover-data/) , and additional property and consumer intent data.


### How can retailers target new homeowners and movers?


Retailers can use new mover and homeowner data to develop audiences of consumers preparing to move, purchasing homes, or settling into new households. These audiences are particularly relevant for furniture, appliances, home improvement, and home goods marketing.


## Conclusion


Today’s retail shopper is connected, value-conscious, mobile-first, and increasingly AI-assisted. Brands that meet them across channels with relevant offers will win more sales and loyalty.
